quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before turning on your engine.
While backing out of your driveway.
When approaching speeds of 55 mph.
When completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before turning on your engine.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, check that all your mirrors are working. Adjust them before you start your engine so you can see clearly without leaning forward or backward.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the pavement, don't panic. Release the accelerator and steer straight. Slow down gradually and gently steer back onto the road using small wheel movements. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before you turn or change lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Don't rely only on mirrors—mirrors alone cannot show everything around your vehicle.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross, as it is unlikely that a train will be coming.
Dangerous.
Safe locations to park a car.
A place where it is required to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead winds a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. When you see this sign, slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and increase your distance from other vehicles.

questions.question: When a drawbridge signal is red, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Quickly speed up.
Proceed with caution.
Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red drawbridge signal means stop at the marked line. The bridge is operating and no vehicles or pedestrians can cross.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains, cars, and bicycles all share the road.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What should you be most concerned about when you see this sign?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto a low shoulder, do not slam on the brakes or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop. Watch for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait until the arm is pulled back.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until the arm is pulled back.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the side with the broken line.
You can pass from the side with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: U-turns are not allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
The road curves ahead.
A sharp left turn is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means that action is prohibited. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are most slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your car to slide and lose grip.
Leave extra space between you and other cars before stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially when rain first starts. Your tires can lose grip on water. You need extra stopping distance on wet pavement. Slow down in rain, standing water, or slush.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T-shaped intersection.
Your road is crossing a divided highway.
You are driving over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road is crossing a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road is about to cross a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate roads going in opposite directions.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the other lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass when it is safe.

questions.question: When you drive faster, your field of vision:

options.text: Gets wider.
Gets narrower.
Makes it easier to see side traffic.
Stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets narrower.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision becomes narrower. Higher speeds mean you see less around you. Be extra alert for hazards when driving fast.

questions.question: If a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever moved first
The driver
Whoever is moving slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at any intersection, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, signal:

options.text: Just as you change lanes.
At any time.
After you change lanes.
Early so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs mean?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians when driving near schools.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.
A traffic light is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic light is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers may keep you awake, but they cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They may drive so badly that they seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually older drivers only.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so badly that they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a flooded road?

options.text: Drive through until the water seems too deep.
Drive through because standing water is usually not deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. You cannot tell how deep the water is or how strong the current is. Your car could be swept away or sink.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there are no other cars.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Always treat them like stop signs.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in the rain.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing, because bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the road is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light will turn red soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive slowly and with care. Look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do at a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there are no other cars.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign forbids it.

questions.question: When you see a car with bright headlights coming toward you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the lights. Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your car back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Slam on your brakes and stop right away.
Gently use the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your car leaves the road, keep driving off the road and slow down gently with the brakes. When you are going slowly enough, turn the steering wheel to get back on the road. Do not turn the wheel sharply to force your car back.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can get all the way through.
Honk your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can get all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side and you cannot get all the way through. Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: How long does a DUI conviction stay on your driving record?

options.text: One year.
10 years.
40 years.
75 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 years.
questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is very dangerous. The penalties are very strict. People who drive after drinking can get heavy fines, higher insurance rates, lose their license, and go to jail. A DUI conviction stays on your driving record for 75 years.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are both on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are both on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: Traffic lights at an intersection are not working because of a power outage. What should you do?

options.text: Park your car as far off the road as possible and wait for the power to come back.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on your hazard lights and go through the intersection without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light is not working because of a power outage, treat the intersection the same way as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the way you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, go through the intersection carefully.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to show what you plan to do.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane as you.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to let other drivers know you plan to change lanes. Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the back of a car if it is in your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, this keeps you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to make sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to make sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look through your back window for people and objects. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially with children nearby. Before you back into or out of a driveway, get out of the car and check behind it.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrived first.
The driver who arrived last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all cars must stop. The first car to reach the intersection should go forward first. If two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers about work zones. This sign tells you that construction is ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, after the train has passed.
Never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad crossings when you see flashing red lights, lowered gates, or a flagging person. Do not go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The full width of a lane, like other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full width of a lane, like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane width, just like cars and trucks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails are ahead and to the right.
A hotel is ahead and to the right.
A hospital is ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hospital is ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where a hospital with emergency services is located.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Drive slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate. Signal, find an opening, and merge into traffic at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.question: How does the type of alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves are ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.
Brake quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: When turning left, which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green left-turn arrow
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green left-turn arrow
questions.explanation: A green left-turn arrow means you can turn left safely. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and predicts problems before they happen.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A roundabout is ahead.
A lane ends. Merge left.
Turn around.
A curve is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A roundabout is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a roundabout ahead. Enter slowly and yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.
